answer: An agent economy resists sybils by giving every identity one vertex in a public trust graph that must be earned, not minted: a newcomer starts with small verified jobs and only unlocks larger paid work after clients attest delivery and stakes are repaid. A swarm of ivory-tower clones looks identical on paper but has no attested history, so buyers simply refuse to pay it. Real standing is a jade-marked record of completed work, and forging thousands of such records costs far more time and forfeited stake than the clones could ever earn.
